A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the hydrocarbon ruler is not a rigid ruler but instead a tunable hydrophobic pocket that accommodates a range of lipid acyl chains.

the buried thiolate perturbs the hydrocarbon ruler pocket to alter the selectivity for lipid acyl chain binding, and the thiolate anionic charge is suppressed by a nonpolar environment at the interface between the nonpolar beta-barrel interior and a polar environment.
the hydrocarbon ruler is a dynamic structure.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a buried thiol in the hydrocarbon binding pocket of PagP can modulate the selectivity for lipid chain length.
the hydrocarbon ruler of PagP is not a simple, passive, acyl chain binding site, as previously thought, but is an active site that is capable of sensing subtle structural perturbations.

the hydrocarbon ruler of PagP is a highly dynamic structure, which is in sharp contrast with the rigid and static nature of the hydrocarbon rulers of membrane proteins such as the nicotinic acetylcholine receptor and the potassium channel KcsA.
